package_info.why_malicious: The report does not analyze or describe any specific malicious package. Instead, it discusses the general risks associated with using open source components that have known vulnerabilities, particularly in the financial services industry. No specific package, code, or technical indicators of malware are provided.

behavioral_signatures: Use of outdated or vulnerable open source dependencies in software projects
Direct downloads of packages from public internet repositories instead of vetted internal repositories
file_indicators: Presence of dependency files (e.g., package.json, requirements.txt, Gemfile) listing outdated or vulnerable package versions
network_indicators: Outbound connections to public package repositories (e.g., npmjs.com, pypi.org, rubygems.org) from build environments or production systems
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Implement automated scanning of software projects to identify dependencies with known vulnerabilities using tools such as SCA (Software Composition Analysis). Enforce policies that restrict the use of outdated or vulnerable packages and require the use of internal, vetted repositories. Monitor build and deployment environments for direct downloads from public package repositories and flag any attempts to bypass internal controls.
